execution.scope: Matched main e46e72e9047ab87488e008494509a4a9129ea5f2 versus integrated candidate 5b2d75403c87d8f3036963e4d868668faff1bcce on MI50 Vulkan. This is a development timing screen, not a correctness gate or merge verdict.

analysis.scope: Matched main/candidate throughput repeat. Candidate/main ratios are descriptive; no acceptance threshold is asserted.

activity.limits: Short-lived processes between samples may be missed; disappeared/new and inaccessible processes are retained as coverage limits. Unavailable GPU counters are not zero.

attribution.method: Processes whose cgroup contains the exact recorded container ID are benchmark; their delta ticks are recomputed between matching PID/start_ticks observations; the activity start-event PID is monitor; all other roles remain as recorded.

analysis.prior_profile_witnesses: Reuse the exact 20 profile witnesses from image-main-timing-v1/collection-01/analysis.json; this repeat adds no profile calls.
limitations: PP and TG reset independently in bench; rates do not represent request latency.
All captured samples are included regardless of activity flags.
Missing intervals, activity counters, process attribution, or profile witnesses remain unknown.

execution.scope: Focused repeated timing of two wide-HF cells with 32 internal bench repetitions per invocation. Matched main/candidate only; no new profile calls. Existing first-pass profiles remain the path witness.

interpretation: Released Q8 mean changes stay within 0.8 percent. The two initially losing tiny-fixture cells were repeated with 32 in-process repetitions per sample: F16-storage/F32 TG changes from -4.67 to +1.68 percent; BF16-storage/BF16 PP changes from -15.44 to -0.87 percent. BF16 repeat TG improves 7.39 percent and F16/F32 repeat PP improves 45.47 percent. These results support retaining the shared policy as a workload tradeoff; they do not claim zero cost or prove the cause of short-run variation.
limitations: Every sample is retained. Background CPU, other-GPU and disk activity is reported. CPU activity attribution uses the exact owned container cgroup; missed short-lived processes remain unknown. PP and TG histories reset independently. This is not a new mx comparison or a completed merge gate.
